description: Apple interviews are unusually team-owned: the same company can run classic LeetCode screens, MLE case studies, hardware verification drills, project deep-dives, and system design loops with little advance disclosure. The strongest pattern is role fit: interviewers probe whether your prior work maps directly to the team's product surface, data domain, and engineering stack, while still expecting clean code, concise trade-off reasoning, and polished behavioral stories.
note: Question block only. The site's answer body is not included here; the untouched page is kept verbatim in raw/<slug>.txt.

questions.title: Sparse Matrix Multiplication (LC 311)
questions.overview: Implement the canonical LC 311 sparse-matrix multiplication task, then explain how to store sparse matrices and avoid unnecessary work on zero entries.

questions.title: Number of Islands
questions.overview: Given a 2D grid grid where '1' represents land and '0' represents water, count and return the number of islands.

questions.title: BST to Sorted Circular Doubly Linked List (LC 426)
questions.overview: Convert a binary search tree in place into a sorted circular doubly linked list, using each node's left pointer as `prev` and right pointer as `next`. Handle an empty tree, connect the final head and tail, and explain or sketch an iterative version.

questions.title: Copy List with Random Pointer (LC 138)
questions.overview: Clone the linked list with random pointers from LC 138, then satisfy an O(1)-auxiliary-space follow-up without corrupting the original list. Pointer restoration and terminal-node handling receive explicit scrutiny.

questions.title: All Nodes Distance K in Binary Tree (LC 863)
questions.overview: Given a binary tree, target node, and distance K, return every node exactly K edges from the target. Follow-ups cover duplicate values, K larger than the tree height, collecting all nodes within K, and avoiding an explicit parent map.

questions.title: Design Hit Counter
questions.overview: Design a hit counter which counts the number of hits received in the past 5 minutes (that is, the past 300 seconds).

questions.title: Top K Closest Pairs in a Sorted Array
questions.overview: Given a sorted array, return the K pairs of values with the smallest absolute differences. The disclosed example uses [1, 2, 4, 7, 11, 16] and asks for the two closest pairs.

questions.title: Insert Interval (LC 57)
questions.overview: Given a sorted list of pairwise non-overlapping intervals and one new interval, insert the new interval, merge any overlaps, and return the sorted non-overlapping result. The Apple round used the canonical LC 57 problem; an Apple-specific modification or follow-up was not disclosed.

questions.title: Merge Intervals
questions.overview: Given an array of intervals where intervals[i] = [starti, endi], merge all overlapping intervals, and return an array of the non-overlapping intervals that cover all the intervals in the input.

questions.title: Alias Group Mapping
questions.overview: Given pairs of words that are bidirectional aliases under a transitive relationship, return a map for every connected alias group. Each key is the lexicographically smallest word in its group, and each value is the group's complete word list in ascending lexicographic order.

questions.title: Subset Sum and All Subsets with Given Sum
questions.overview: Two-part phone-screen prompt: given an array and a target, first decide whether any subset sums to the target using DP with space optimized to O(target) and O(n * target) time; then return all subsets that sum to the target via backtracking in O(2^n) time, with a space-complexity analysis.

questions.title: Hotel Booking System OOD Coding
questions.overview: Design and implement a small hotel booking system with availability checks and room booking over date ranges, then discuss how to prevent conflicting bookings under concurrency.

questions.title: Binary Tree Vertical Order Traversal
questions.overview: Given the root of a binary tree, return the vertical order traversal of its nodes' values.

questions.title: Valid Sudoku
questions.overview: Validate whether a partially filled Sudoku board is legal by checking every row, every column, and every 3x3 sub-grid for duplicate digits.

questions.title: Top K Frequent Elements
questions.overview: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, return the k most frequent elements. You may return the answer in any order.

questions.title: Happy Number Service
questions.overview: Implement a service that decides whether a positive integer is a happy number, then scale it to billions of requests.

questions.title: Reconstruct Itinerary
questions.overview: You are given a list of airline tickets where tickets[i] = [fromi, toi] represent the departure and the arrival airports of one flight. Reconstruct the itinerary in order and return it.

questions.title: Shortest Path in a Grid with Obstacle Removal
questions.overview: BFS shortest path from a start cell to an end cell in a grid with blocked cells, with a follow-up that lets you convert blocked cells to open ones.

questions.title: Rotate Image
questions.overview: You are given an n x n 2D matrix representing an image. Rotate the image by 90 degrees clockwise, in place.

questions.title: Kubernetes Service Filter & Dependency Chain
questions.overview: Implement filters over Kubernetes service records, then compute dependency chains and query status along the chain. A final open-ended follow-up asks how to expose the code as an MCP server for agents while reducing noise.

questions.title: Odd Even Linked List
questions.overview: Given the head of a singly linked list, group all nodes at odd indices together followed by the nodes at even indices, and return the reordered list.

questions.title: Bag-of-Words Similarity Search from Scratch
questions.overview: This Apple Machine Learning Engineer phone screen asks you to build a tiny similarity search engine using the bag-of-words (BoW) representation, from scratch, without scikit-learn or any vectorizer library.

questions.title: Substring Pattern Matches
questions.overview: Given a string s and a non-empty pattern pattern, return every starting index i in s where the substring s[i..i + pattern.length - 1] equals pattern.

questions.title: Valid Palindrome
questions.overview: Given a string s, return true if it is a palindrome, otherwise return false.

questions.title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock
questions.overview: You are given an integer array prices where prices[i] is the price of NeetCoin on the ith day.

questions.title: Cheapest Flights Within K Stops
questions.overview: There are n cities connected by some flights. You are given an array flights where flights[i] = [fromi, toi, pricei] indicates a flight from city fromi to city toi with cost pricei.

questions.title: Search a 2D Matrix
questions.overview: You are given an m x n integer matrix matrix with the following two properties:.

questions.title: Maximum Apples Before Rot
questions.overview: Each day an apple tree grows `apples[i]` apples that rot after `days[i]`; eat at most one apple per day and maximize total apples eaten, including days after growth stops.

questions.title: Flood Fill
questions.overview: You are given an m x n integer grid image where image[r][c] is the pixel color at that position, and three integers sr, sc, and color.

questions.title: Merge Two Sorted Lists
questions.overview: You are given the heads of two sorted linked lists list1 and list2.

questions.title: Bus Route Earliest Arrival
questions.overview: Given bus routes / schedules, travel times between stops, waiting times, origin, destination, and departure time, compute the earliest arrival time.

questions.title: Koko Eating Bananas
questions.overview: Koko loves to eat bananas. There are n piles of bananas, the i\-th pile has piles[i] bananas. The guards have gone and will come back in h hours.

questions.title: Implement TF-IDF from Scratch
questions.overview: This is an Apple Machine Learning Engineer phone screen Tech1 coding round.

questions.title: LRU Cache
questions.overview: Design a data structure that follows the constraints of a Least Recently Used (LRU) cache.

questions.title: Container With Most Water
questions.overview: You are given an integer array heights where heights[i] represents the height of the ithi^{th}ith bar.

questions.title: Product of Array Except Self
questions.overview: Given an integer array nums, return an array output where output[i] is the product of all the elements of nums except nums[i].

questions.title: Merge K Sorted Lists
questions.overview: You are given an array of k linked lists lists, where each list is sorted in ascending order.

questions.title: Longest Mountain in Array
questions.overview: You may recall that an array arr is a mountain array if and only if:.

questions.title: Trapping Rain Water
questions.overview: Given n non-negative integers representing an elevation map where the width of each bar is 1, compute how much water it can trap after raining.

questions.title: Query Image Similarity Search
questions.overview: This is a recent Apple onsite Round 4 ML Coding task for Machine Learning Engineer candidates.

questions.title: Course Schedule
questions.overview: You are given an array prerequisites where prerequisites[i] = [a, b] indicates that you must take course b first if you want to take course a.

questions.title: LFU Cache
questions.overview: Design and implement a data structure for a Least Frequently Used (LFU) cache.

questions.title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock II
questions.overview: You are given an integer array prices where prices[i] is the price of a given stock on the ith day.

questions.title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
questions.overview: Given a string s, find the length of the longest substring without duplicate characters.

questions.title: Bold Words in String
questions.overview: Given an array of keywords words and a string s, make all appearances of all keywords words[i] in s bold. Any letters between and tags become bold.

questions.title: Implement Trie (Prefix Tree)
questions.overview: A prefix tree (also known as a trie) is a tree data structure used to efficiently store and retrieve keys in a set of strings. Some applications of this data structure include auto-complete and spell checker systems.

questions.title: Intersection of Two Linked Lists
questions.overview: Given the heads of two singly linked lists headA and headB, return the node at which the two lists intersect. If the two lists have no intersection, return null.

questions.title: Kth Largest Element in an Array
questions.overview: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, return the kth largest element in the array.

questions.title: Write a Debounce Function
questions.overview: Implement a debounce(fn, wait) utility in JavaScript.

questions.title: Deck Shuffle and Draw OOD
questions.overview: Design `Card` and `Deck` classes that support shuffle and draw with correct probabilities. The prompt is OOD-shaped but the algorithmic core is random sampling without replacement.

questions.title: UNet Debugging for Image MLE
questions.overview: Image / video MLE phone screen asking ML concepts plus a PyTorch UNet debugging task: fix tensor shape, decoder boolean, final kernel size, and number of classes.

questions.title: Redundant Connection
questions.overview: In this problem, a tree is an undirected graph that is connected and has no cycles.

questions.title: Decode String
questions.overview: Given an encoded string, return its decoded string.

questions.title: One Edit Distance
questions.overview: Given two strings s and t, return true if they are both exactly one edit distance apart, otherwise return false.

questions.title: Dedupe Unsorted Array (Three Variants)
questions.overview: You are given a method that takes in an array of unsorted integers and you must return the deduped array. The interviewer runs it as three progressively tighter variants, using each one to gauge a different skill:.

questions.title: Valid Parentheses
questions.overview: You are given a string s consisting of the following characters: '(', ')', '{', '}', '[' and ']'.

questions.title: Find Median (Oracle Variant)
questions.overview: You are asked to find the median of an unseen array nums of n distinct or repeating integers. You cannot read the array directly — instead, you are given three oracle operations:.

questions.title: Serialize and Deserialize Binary Tree
questions.overview: Implement an algorithm to serialize and deserialize a binary tree.

questions.title: Zero Out Duplicates and Sort Without Native Sort
questions.overview: Given an unsorted integer array of about 75 elements with duplicates, zero out duplicate values and sort the data without using native sort, quicksort, or bubble sort.

questions.title: Lazy Binary Tree Inorder Iterator
questions.overview: Design an iterator over a binary tree that returns nodes in inorder sequence without precomputing all values. The follow-up asks about multiple iterators and thread safety.

questions.title: Subarray Sum Equals K
questions.overview: Given an integer array and target `k`, count all contiguous subarrays whose sum equals `k`. The follow-up checks whether negative numbers break sliding-window assumptions.

questions.title: Find K Pairs with Smallest Sums
questions.overview: You are given two integer arrays nums1 and nums2 sorted in non-decreasing order, and an integer k.

questions.title: Permutations
questions.overview: Given an array nums of distinct integers, return all possible permutations. You can return the answer in any order.

questions.title: Airplane Seat Reservation API
questions.overview: Implement a C-style airplane seating API with create, print, free, and reserve functions. The reserve call parses seats like `4B` and may choose an alternate seat when movement is allowed.

questions.title: Group Anagrams
questions.overview: Given an array of strings strs, group all anagrams together into sublists. You may return the output in any order.

questions.title: Insert Delete GetRandom O(1)
questions.overview: Implement the RandomizedSet class:.

questions.title: Numbers with No Neighbors
questions.overview: Given an integer array nums, return every value n in nums that satisfies both conditions:.

questions.title: Out of Boundary Paths
questions.overview: There is an m x n grid with a ball. The ball starts at [startRow, startColumn]. On each move, the ball can move to an adjacent cell in one of four directions.

questions.title: Number of Islands II
questions.overview: You are given an empty m x n grid initially filled with water. We may perform an addLand operation where positions[i] = [ri, ci] turns the cell (ri, ci) into land.

questions.title: Online Token Processing, Embeddings, and Classification
questions.overview: This is an Apple Machine Learning Engineer phone screen (Round 2). The interviewer gives you a stream of labeled text records and asks you to build an end-to-end pipeline that:.

questions.title: Count Value Occurrences in a Binary Tree
questions.overview: You are given the root of a binary tree (not a BST, just a generic binary tree) and a target value x. Count how many nodes in the tree have node.val == x.

questions.title: Implement an Image Filter
questions.overview: This is a recent Apple onsite ML Coding round (Round 3, 20 minutes of coding after 20 minutes of project plus ML fundamentals).

questions.title: Shortest Bridge (Distance Between Two Islands)
questions.overview: You are given a binary grid containing exactly two islands, where 1 is land and 0 is water.

questions.title: Failed Login Log Ranking
questions.overview: Parse system logs, extract failed login attempts, group by IP and machine, and sort by failed-attempt count.

questions.title: Design a HashMap
questions.overview: Design and implement a HashMap<K, V> from scratch, without using the language's built-in hash map. Support the standard API:.

questions.title: Weighted Random Load Balancer IP
questions.overview: Given a list of load-balancer IPs, return a random IP uniformly; then extend to weighted probability where higher-weight IPs are chosen more often.

questions.title: Transformer Attention Mask and Heads Coding
questions.overview: Apple AIML / MLE rounds can ask live ML coding around Transformer internals: implement or debug attention, add heads, add masks, and reason about tensor shapes.

questions.title: Vectorized K-Means in NumPy or PyTorch
questions.overview: Implement K-means with tensor operations rather than Python loops. Interviewers care about broadcasting, `unsqueeze`, `keepdim`, centroid updates, and whether the implementation stays efficient.

questions.title: Object Storage / Dropbox / S3 Design
questions.overview: A recurring storage-system design family covering Dropbox-style file sync, S3-style object storage, and storage-team fundamentals.

questions.title: Cross-Device Wallpaper Synchronization
questions.overview: Design wallpaper exchange and synchronization across a user's devices. Cover opportunistic prefetching, resumable downloads, version detection, cache priority, concurrent updates, retry behavior, and the split between background work and main-thread UI commits.

questions.title: Large-Scale Media Transfer to ML Compute
questions.overview: Design a one-time transfer of 200 TB of images and video from an on-premises source to a cloud GPU training cluster within a few days. Compare physical and network migration, use an object-store landing zone, preserve integrity and security, and extend the design into a recurring ingestion and GPU input pipeline.

questions.title: Log Processing System
questions.overview: Design a log processing system that ingests a continuous stream of application logs from a large service fleet and counts errors in real time. A dashboard and alerting layer sits on top, so error counts must be accurate and available with low latency.

questions.title: Design a RAG-Based Chatbot System
questions.overview: Design an intelligent chatbot system that uses Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to answer user queries.

questions.title: Design ChatGPT
questions.overview: Design a conversational AI system like ChatGPT: users send text prompts and receive AI-generated responses streamed back token-by-token, with persistent conversation history across sessions.

questions.title: Design App Store Search
questions.overview: Design the search system for the Apple App Store.

questions.title: Design a Chat Application
questions.overview: Design a chat application that supports one-on-one and group messaging with user registration, real-time message delivery, and offline support.

questions.title: Design News Feed
questions.overview: Design a news feed system: users follow other users and see a reverse-chronological (or ranked) feed of posts from the people they follow, with support for posting, likes, and real-time-ish delivery at very large scale.

questions.title: Design TTL Cache
questions.overview: Design a cache where every entry has a time-to-live (TTL): it is readable for a fixed window after insertion, then disappears.

questions.title: Apple News Search (No ML)
questions.overview: Design the first version of search for Apple News. A user types a free-form query (e.g. "tesla earnings", "wildfires california") and expects back a ranked list of news articles drawn from tens of thousands of publishers.

questions.title: Design (key, value) Storage with Snapshots
questions.overview: Design a key-value store that supports point-in-time snapshots.

questions.title: Design a Concurrent Image Upload System
questions.overview: Design a system like Craigslist that accepts a list of images and stores them concurrently, updating the user about the status of each upload as soon as possible.

questions.title: Distributed Task Scheduler
questions.overview: Storage infra onsite design for a distributed task scheduler, with follow-ups on queue structure, task representation, and scaling.

questions.title: Distributed Rate Limiter with Lua Details
questions.overview: Storage infra onsite system design asking for a distributed rate limiter, with interviewer emphasis on implementation detail such as Redis Lua scripting.

questions.title: Ad Click Aggregator
questions.overview: Design an ads click aggregation pipeline. The Apple version emphasizes multiple data sources such as web, mobile, and TV, plus click-count accuracy.

questions.title: Siri Grounded Response Generation
questions.overview: Design or case-study a Siri response-generation system where answers must stay grounded in tool results, avoid hallucination, fit a voice-chat length budget, and remain evaluable as context grows.

questions.title: Behavioral Prioritization and Stakeholder Fit
questions.overview: Common Apple behavioral / HM prompts: end-to-end ownership, difficult debugging, a mistaken technical decision, disagreement and collaboration, why Apple, work style, prioritization, stakeholder blockers, and measurable project impact. Debugging stories may be probed down to the logs inspected, how the search space narrowed, and why the first hypothesis failed.

questions.title: ML Fundamentals & Model Debugging Drill
questions.overview: Apple MLE loops repeatedly include verbal drills on model choice, evaluation, data processing, LLM concepts, ranking / ads models, GPU OOM, and production metric drops.

questions.title: ML Systems Codebase Deep Dive
questions.overview: A no-coding HM technical screen for an ML Systems Engineer role that turns into a deep review of one recent project and its codebase. The interviewer probes architecture, deployment, data collection, cross-evaluation, database choices, agentic-system rationale, FastAPI / LangGraph state handling, PDF embedding, similarity search, and paper retrieval.

questions.title: OS Fundamentals & Concurrency Drill
questions.overview: Apple Core OS / low-level teams open with a hiring-manager round that stays almost entirely on OS fundamentals: process vs thread, CPU scheduling, synchronization primitives (mutex / semaphore / condition variable), race conditions and deadlock, escalating to multi-core synchronization.

questions.title: SystemVerilog DV Constraint & Architecture Loop
questions.overview: Hardware DV intern loop covering SystemVerilog constraints, UVM-style testbench components, edge detectors, assertions, virtual functions, semaphores / mailboxes, architecture fundamentals, and Python sorting.

questions.title: Accessories QA Benchmark and Regression Deep Dive
questions.overview: Present prior QA projects and explain regression reliability, benchmark evaluation, HPC resource use, and runtime improvements. Follow-ups probe whether pass/fail results capture failure severity and who decides whether performance deviations are acceptable.

questions.title: Frontend React Screen
questions.overview: Frontend phone screen covering React fundamentals, CSS concepts, UI troubleshooting, component structure, and sometimes a coding warm-up such as merge intervals or debounce.
